pairs.question: Saeuos Amor docuit natorum sanguine matrem commaculare manus; crudelis tu quoque, mater: crudelis mater magis, an puer improbus ille?
pairs.answer: Improbus ille puer; crudelis tu quoque, mater.
pairs.derivation: Disjunctive interrogative (crudelis mater magis, an puer improbus ille?) self-answered in the next line. Setup retained from the start of the sentence (Saeuos Amor docuit... commaculare manus; crudelis tu quoque, mater) so 'ille puer' (Amor/Cupid) and 'mater' (Medea) have referents and the comparison is intelligible. Answer is the full retort line; nothing cut from it. The verse-refrain lines (Incipe Maenalios...) flanking this stanza are stripped as scaffolding, as are the dangling inline line-numbers.
